description: The >>TURN { exception-name [file-name]... }... { CHECKING ON [WITH LOCATION] | CHECKING OFF } compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.25) - it enables and disables exception checking for the source text that follows. Recognized and parsed by TurnDirectiveProcessor into the TurnEvent list the checking model reads; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002 through the ONE ConstructRegistry funnel - it emitted a bespoke COBOL0875 until kb/Work PB725, which RETIRED that code (never reallocate). The §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction: COBOL-85 has no compiler directives at all, so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source. The edition edge below 2023 is DERIVED, not quoted (VCR Table 7's discipline, rows 7.19/7.20 - the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): the derivation is (a) the M2 post-85 feature catalog in docs/ISO2023_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md, which places '*>' inline comments, >>SOURCE FORMAT, conditional compilation and 'recognize-and-ignore of the other standard >> directives' in COBOL-2002, (b) the sibling row leap-second-directive-2002, already landed on the same derivation (kb/Work PB65), and (c) Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does NOT list this directive among the additions, so it predates 2023. Overturnable in one line if the 2002/2014 text is ever acquired.
citation: ISO §2023:7.3.25; the §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction (M2 catalog derivation, VCR Table 7 discipline)

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.25.2 general format + §2023:7.3.25.3 SR1/SR3/SR4: an exception-name list with optional file-names and a CHECKING phrase — a structured operand, diagnosed by its own stage as COBOL0718/COBOL0719.

source:
>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725TU.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
